question: Should native Codex app-server models ship default API-style dollar pricing, or should nonzero Codex cost estimates require explicit authoritative pricing or billing-mode proof?
rationale: The code can be repaired either way, but the default affects existing users' billing interpretation for subscription-backed Codex turns and conflicts with the previously closed Codex cost-authority issue unless maintainers choose a billing-mode contract.

options.title: Gate estimates by billing mode
options.body: Keep native subscription-backed Codex usage non-authoritative by default and allow nonzero estimates only when explicit pricing or API-key billing context proves pay-per-token spend.

options.title: Remove static Codex prices
options.body: Treat native Codex pricing as unknown/missing unless a user or pricing cache provides real rates, preserving current subscription semantics but not estimating API-key Codex spend by default.

options.title: Accept static Codex estimates
options.body: Ship the default rates intentionally, but document that they are estimates and add proof that subscription-backed users will not confuse them with authoritative billed spend.

recommendation.title: Gate estimates by billing mode
recommendation.body: Keep native subscription-backed Codex usage non-authoritative by default and allow nonzero estimates only when explicit pricing or API-key billing context proves pay-per-token spend.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex provider and OpenAI identity history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the billing/default-pricing direction.
